findings.summary: The site does not follow the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot remains the same white surface as light mode; computed `color-scheme` is `normal`, and the 339 KB stylesheet has zero prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare `color-scheme: light dark` and define preference-driven surface, text, border, and form-control colors with `prefers-color-scheme` or `light-dark()`.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero view-transition rules across the shared stylesheet; this MPA changes between core routes without cross-document transition styling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` with restrained shared-element styling, preserving the reduced-motion treatment.

findings.summary: Long pages do not provide scroll-state-aware navigation chrome.
findings.evidence: The 6,259 px home page uses static header/navigation chrome; CSS inspection found no scroll-state queries or scroll-timeline support.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky, compact header or progress/scroll affordance driven by scroll-state/container queries, without obscuring content.

findings.summary: Dropdown and menu positioning relies on legacy custom/Bootstrap behavior rather than anchored positioning.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection shows dropdown/collapse controls but no popover, anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage in the shared shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Move transient menus/tooltips to popover plus CSS anchor positioning and provide position-try fallbacks near viewport edges.

findings.summary: Shared disclosure and menu controls use custom collapse markup instead of modern semantic primitives.
findings.evidence: The rendered shell has zero dialog/popover elements; mobile footer disclosures are buttons wired through data-toggle collapse rather than details, and menus use custom dropdown markup.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `<details>` for footer disclosures and popover/dialog for transient/modal UI, preserving names, focus, and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Components respond only through viewport-era CSS rather than their own containers.
findings.evidence: The 339 KB shared stylesheet contains zero `@container` rules; reusable cards and result/filter components are therefore coupled to global breakpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce `container-type: inline-size` on reusable regions and local `@container` rules for cards, result/filter layouts, and dense navigation.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance misses the Core Web Vitals bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 11.1 s, FCP 4.2 s, Speed Index 7.1 s, and CLS 0.154 (performance 0.54); an independent trace measured LCP 5.22 s and FCP 3.67 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, compress text and images, reduce render-blocking work, and reserve all media space; verify under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Late content shifts exceed the stable-layout target.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded CLS 0.154 with two shift clusters; 11 of 12 images lacked explicit dimensions, while a separate mobile layout observation still recorded CLS 0.022 after waiting.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and reserve carousel/widget space before resources arrive.

findings.summary: Critical resources are large, uncompressed, cache-poor, and render-blocking.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 2.66 MB: 1.55 MB script, 383 KB CSS, and 658 KB images. The 614 KB classic aeat.07.js has neither async nor defer; large text resources were uncompressed and many images/scripts lacked cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Compress text with Brotli, defer non-critical classic scripts, split/inline only critical CSS, add immutable caching for versioned assets, and optimize LCP image discovery.

findings.summary: Most shipped JavaScript and CSS is unused on the landing page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 864 KiB unused JavaScript and 358 KiB unused CSS; two first-party scripts alone transferred about 1.25 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the shared bundle by route/component, remove obsolete code, and load the click-to-call integration only when the user invokes it.

findings.summary: Shared controls have invalid or missing accessible names/relationships.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility found the Area personal link has no discernible name and four footer buttons have aria-controls values that reference nonexistent IDs.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the account link an accessible name and make every disclosure button’s aria-controls exactly match an existing panel ID; keep aria-expanded synchronized.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on several shared controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found no outline or focus box-shadow on the language button, mobile-menu button, search submit button, carousel CTA, or next-slide control, while many links did receive a yellow focus ring.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a consistent high-contrast `:focus-visible` ring to every interactive element and verify a complete keyboard walk.

findings.summary: Image sizing and delivery have avoidable quality defects.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 11 images without dimensions, 3 oversized images, 6 legacy-format images, and 5 without responsive sources; Lighthouse also flagged an incorrect call-widget aspect ratio and low-resolution icons.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions and responsive `srcset`/`sizes`, preserve aspect ratios, and replace photographic PNG/JPEG assets with right-sized AVIF/WebP variants.

findings.summary: Large first-party scripts lack valid source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported missing source maps for the 614 KB aeat.07.js and 635 KB clickC.js assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish production source maps with controlled access or remove stale sourceMappingURL references; use them to diagnose remaining bundle waste.

findings.summary: Key public pages lack meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: Route metadata found no description on the home or Contacta con nosotros pages; Lighthouse failed the home meta-description audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add concise, unique descriptions that state the page purpose and primary service for every indexable template.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: None of five representative pages exposed a canonical link; `/sitemap.xml` returned 404, while robots.txt lists only disallow rules and no sitemap location.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit self-referencing canonicals on public templates and publish an XML sitemap referenced from robots.txt; retain NOINDEX only for internal search results.

findings.summary: Public entity and content templates lack structured/share metadata.
findings.evidence: Across home, IRPF, registration, contact, and search templates, the probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and template-specific structured data where applicable, plus Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: Analytics cookies are set without Secure and with SameSite=None.
findings.evidence: Cookie evidence found both `_ga` cookies lacked Secure, used SameSite=None, and persisted for 400 days. HTTPS and HSTS are present, but the cookie posture weakens the transport baseline.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure and an appropriate SameSite value for all cookies, shorten analytics lifetime, and verify consent/necessity before setting analytics identifiers.

findings.summary: Tracking starts on page load with a persistent analytics footprint.
findings.evidence: The load contacted four third-party origins including Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics, transferred 302 KB third-party data, and set 400-day `_ga` identifiers; no consent interaction preceded the requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize or remove client analytics, gate non-essential tracking behind an explicit choice where required, and use short-lived, privacy-preserving first-party measurement.

findings.summary: The CSP and defensive header set are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows CSP contains only `frame-ancestors`; X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent. HSTS and clickjacking controls are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based resource CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a strict Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy, testing in report-only mode first.

findings.summary: The shared layout is not robust for bidirectional writing modes.
findings.evidence: The site provides multiple language variants and sets lang=es, but the 339 KB stylesheet contains 1,007 physical left/right property occurrences and only one logical-property occurrence; no dir attribute is emitted.
findings.suggestedFix: Use inline/block logical properties and emit the correct `dir` per locale so translated layouts can support RTL without template forks.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and misses responsive optimization.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 3 oversized images, 6 legacy-format assets, 5 images without srcset, and 6 below-fold images without lazy loading; the 1,125 px QR is displayed at 80 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP sources, right-size the QR and carousel assets, and lazy-load below-fold media with intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Third-party and decorative resources are disproportionate to this mostly informational page.
findings.evidence: The page transfers 2.66 MB, including 302 KB third-party code, a 380 KB carousel JPEG, and more than 1.2 MB of first-party script; several below-fold assets load eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level byte budget, defer third-party/click-to-call code until needed, and lazy-load non-critical visual media.
